checked.label: 12 weeks (retag to dependent)
checked.notes: Retag confirmed. Hser 2017 full text (PMC5607644 via NCBI efetch, read 2026-11-08): 'In the parent study (ACCENT), 302 adults (ages 18–50) with a diagnosis of cannabis dependence (per DSM-IV ... criteria) were randomized'. So the trial required dependence: severity 'dependent', Counted 'people hooked on weed, in a treatment trial' (has 'hooked', 8 words) is right, and matches belief 4. F3: headline says it counted using less ('people who smoked on fewer days; quitters were not counted on their own'), Weak 'Using less, not quitting; small changes', caveat opens 'This is using less, not stopping' and ends on the 71 in 100 pointer. Abstract confirms n 302, 152 reduction vs 150 increase, 12-week trial.

checked.notes: Connor 2022 abstract re-read 2026-11-08 (Europe PMC): 'most symptoms generally peak at days 2-6, with some symptoms lasting up to 3 weeks or more in heavy cannabis users' is word for word. The proof now agrees with the Day 2–6 card (peak days 2–6, most lasted 4–14 days) and the body rows (irritable still there at week 4; sleep to day 45): 'some last up to 3 weeks or more' and 'poor sleep ... several weeks or longer' fit both. No line gives a competing 'usual' length. 2 figures. Answers 'barely lasted three days' (day 3 sits in the peak).
